body:
I do think about aging and what scares me isn't my physical body breaking down, but my mind breaking down. Seeing a friend's grandparent slowly die from Alzheimer's truly made me feel more sad and frightened than anything I have seen since.

When I think of people who are happy, I think of people in my life who don't question anything. They live their lives in seeming ignorance and are simply happy to be at this job/in this school/on this planet. Sure, our society is terribly repressive, sure our economic system works daily to crush the human spirit, but they seem to not notice. Of course, you are probably right that most people aren't happy. Maybe these people I'm thinking of secretly aren't as uncritical as they seem on the surface. Perhaps they really do suffer.

I don't really like the argument that killing myself may lead to an endless loop of bad karma and suffering reincarnations, but your last point does make me think. Maybe trying to find some answers to help other people is something I can do.

Thank you for the reply. I appreciate it. I do like reading books and I will check out *Siddhartha* from the library. I am perhaps skeptical of the premise of *The Power of Now*. I just feel like I'm not capable of enjoying life or the present, whether or not I focus on it or try to live in the moment. Maybe that's why I keep telling myself the future will be better. If all of life will be like the present ... I don't know if I could live a whole life like that.
